display.title: Mitzvah Time: The Kavanah of 'Echad' in the Shema
display.summary_short: What to think when saying 'Echad' in the Shema: Hashem is the one Master of the seven heavens, the earth and all four directions.
display.summary_long: A short Mitzvah Time lesson from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Uncle Yossi explains that besides saying the words of the Shema, we must have the right kavanah, the right thought in mind. Beyond its simple meaning, 'one', the Gemara teaches that each letter of the word Echad carries a special meaning. The aleph stands for Hashem, the one Master and Ruler. The ches has the value eight: the seven heavens Hashem placed around the world, plus the earth. The dalet has the value four: north, south, east and west. So when we say Echad, we picture that Hashem rules up above, down below and in every direction: Hashem is truly everywhere.
display.lesson: When you say 'Echad', think that Hashem is the one Master of everything: up, down and all around.
